title: Enforce row-level scope and attribute-based filters for console usage views
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The console exposes multi-tenant usage views and time-series endpoints that power cost/latency dashboards and export jobs. Currently, authorization is coarse-grained and applied at the endpoint level, which permits queries to return rows outside a requesting principal's effective scope when downstream code applies additional filters. That leads to potential data leakage risk and forces expensive post-query filtering in application code.

Goal: Implement a tenant-aware, attribute-based projection and row-level enforcement layer that pushes permission predicates into analytics query planning so that only permitted rows/columns are scanned and returned. This layer should integrate with the existing entitlement service and respect role -> tenant -> attribute mappings (e.g., account_id, org_unit, project_ids, environment tags).

Why now: We are scaling export frequency and serving more cross-tenant aggregated views. SLOs for query latency and resource utilization are degrading due to broad scans that are later filtered. Security audit flagged two near-miss incidents where an edge case in post-filtering could have exposed rows.

Out-of-scope: Changing data model or full reimplementation of analytics storage. This ticket focuses on authorization plumbing, query predicate synthesis, and conservative planner hooks that operate before materialization or aggregation where feasible.
acceptance_criteria: Policy enforcement layer (PDP) attaches a deterministic SQL predicate for every analytics query representing the caller's effective row/column scope and is consumed by the query planner.
All console usage endpoints (timeseries, exports, raw-usage) must reject requests where the PDP cannot produce a finite predicate (explicit error code 403-UNSCOPED).
Query planner uses predicate to prune partitions and early-exit for empty scopes (no rows scanned). Measured decrease in average scanned partitions by >=40% on test traffic.
Unit and integration tests for attribute mappings for at least three typical roles (admin, billing-user, read-only-tenant) with mock entitlements.
Audit events emitted for each authorization decision referencing policy version and resolved predicate string.
Performance regression: p95 endpoint latency for timeseries queries does not increase by more than 10% in staging with PDP enabled; p50 should improve for large-tenant scopes.
Rollout toggle present (feature flag) to enable/disable predicate-push per route and per-customer for emergency rollback.
technical_design: Introduce an Authorization Projection component (AP) in console-backend analytics route pipeline that: resolves caller attributes from token + entitlements service, fetches policy from PDP, synthesizes a predicate expression in our query DSL, and attaches metadata to request context.

PDP integration: use existing entitlement APIs (ENG-60500) but add a new /pdp/resolve endpoint that returns: {policy_id, version, predicate_dsl, deny_reasons}. For compatibility the AP will fall back to endpoint-level checks when PDP returns no predicate but mark request for manual review.

Query planner changes: accept predicate_dsl and translate into storage-layer filters (partition keys, timestamp ranges, attribute equality/IN conditions). Add a fast path for 'empty-scope' predicates that immediately return a 200 with empty payload for streaming endpoints.
Caching: cache resolved predicate strings keyed by (subject, route, projection-hash, PDP-version) with TTL 5m. Evict on policy-change webhook (policy service emits policy-version updates).
Auditing: log structured audit entries to analytics-audit topic with fields: request_id, subject_id, policy_id, policy_version, predicate_hash, route, decision, timestamp.

Security: reject predicates derived from untrusted attributes (client-provided) unless verified by entitlement service. All predicates must be sanitized with a whitelist of supported operators to avoid injection attacks.
Feature flag: implement ff in launchdarkly key 'analytics.pdp_projection_push' with per-customer override in the dedicated/private reconcile pipeline.
Backwards compatibility: endpoints will accept both 'legacy' (post-filtering) and 'pdp' modes; tests and migration plan will convert high-risk customers gradually.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Enable PDP projection push for 100% staging traffic. Run full integration tests and measure partition scans. Duration: 1 week.
Phase 2 (canary): Enable for 5 internal customers (low-risk). Monitor errors, audit logs, and latency, and validate exports. Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (gradual): Incrementally ramp to 25%, 50%, 100% for hosted customers with automated rollback on increased 5xx or audit mismatch signals.
Phase 4 (enterprise): Engage account teams to test on Dedicated/Private customers; provide migration checklist and enable per-customer opt-in.
Emergency rollback: FF off + clear predicate cache + a short-circuit that marks in-flight requests to run legacy post-filtering path.
migration_steps: Add PDP resolve endpoint and AP component behind feature flag; ship as non-default.
Run analytics jobs in staging to compare predicate-pushed results vs legacy post-filtered results; write differential reports to /tmp/pdp-diffs.
For customers with deterministic matches, enable the FF in canary mode; for mismatches, create follow-up tickets enumerating root causes.
When stable, flip default for hosted tiers and notify Dedicated/Private customers with migration guide.
observability: Dashboards: new 'PDP Projection' dashboard showing: predicate cache hit rate, avg predicate synthesis latency, partition-scan reduction %, mismatch count (predicate vs post-filter), PDP error rate.
Alerts: >2% query failures with 403-UNSCOPED in production for 10m -> paging oncall; >10% increase in p95 latency for timeseries routes -> page.
Tracing: attach predicate_id and policy_version to existing request traces so that the serving runtime can correlate kernel selection impact with effective scope.
Audit sink: new analytics-audit topic consumed by SIEM and retention 1 year for compliance teams.
Export validation: nightly job that replays a sample of queries with legacy post-filtering and compares results to PDP-pruned results to detect silent mismatches.
